_meta.source: bench-eink/analysis/A1_rederived.jsonl (48 tonefine, 4 edges, 4 linepairs, 2 resample, 2 surround)
_meta.units: camera-RGB normalised to THIS panel's own black=0 / white=255 - NOT sRGB
_meta.rule: nothing below its 95% MDD is reported as a finding

corrections_to_the_data.what: wp=0 means the white-point lever is OFF (eink_bench applies it only when wp>0), so wp0 and wp1.0 are BIT-IDENTICAL renders
corrections_to_the_data.evidence: null check across 6 metrics, every difference inside its bar (max: max_chroma -8.32 vs MDD 10.6)
corrections_to_the_data.consequence: the white-point axis is four levels (1.0/0.88/0.75/0.64), and pooling wp0 with wp1.0 is what gives the uncompressed corner any replication

corrections_to_the_data.what: tonefine steps 11, 12, 24, 25 (the last two columns of each grid row) sample the white surround, not the patch
evidence: mean out_lum by step: 90.4 (10) -> 212.6 (11) -> 235.9 (12) -> 123.0 (13); a monotone ramp cannot do that
deviation from a 5-step rolling median 91 and 101 at steps 11,12 vs 0-16 elsewhere
correlates with align dx at r=-0.55 (step 12) and -0.66 (step 25)

invalidates.ramp_span: 47 of 48 rows take their max from a contaminated step - UNUSABLE
invalidates.grain_peak: ~50% of rows take their peak from a contaminated step - do not report
invalidates.collapsed_step_pairs: inflated, and inflated most in the brightest conditions

corrections_to_the_data.fix: drop steps 11,12,24,25; use the two contiguous runs 0-10 and 13-23. Halves sigma on mean grain (2.29->1.42) and monotone pairs (1.72->1.31)

corrections_to_the_data.what: readout_edges 'asymmetry' is a CONTRAST readout, not a diffusion readout
corrections_to_the_data.evidence: on the perfectly registered DIGITAL render, asymmetry = rendered(fg) - rendered(bg) exactly, for all 8 blocks (+220.1=255.0-34.9, -189.0=66.0-255.0, ...), alternating sign with the target's own i%2 polarity flip
corrections_to_the_data.consequence: worst_asymmetry is the target's largest designed contrast, not a smear. edges cannot answer its question.

corrections_to_the_data.what: a +26/255 grid-ROW term contaminates every level read from the tonefine grid
corrections_to_the_data.evidence: within fixed digital-level bins, row1-row0 = +26.0, +31.9, +28.4, +26.7, +13.8 across five bins with n=100-200 each
corrections_to_the_data.unresolved: row and level are perfectly confounded inside any one condition; cannot separate gradient / surround / condition

error_bars_reproduced._note: pooled within (wp_eff,gamma) identical-render groups, n>=3, 32 df; A1 value in brackets

error_bars_new_clean_metrics._basis: clean 22 steps, two contiguous runs, 32 df

findings.claim: Collapse is TWO opposite phenomena; the shipped metric adds them and cancels the main effects
The wp x gamma INTERACTION on highlight collapse is the largest structured effect in the tone data: white-point only buys anything at low gamma
Grain climbs with gamma and with compression - but grain_peak shows NOTHING; the honest carrier is grain_hi
findings.overturns: the brief's preliminary read 'grain_peak 30 -> 63 -> 98' - that is one un-randomised row of a contaminated metric

findings.claim: GRAIN IS A FUNCTION OF WHERE THE TONE LANDS, NOT OF WHICH LEVER PUT IT THERE. Peak at digital ~55, decaying to ~2 at the white ink (163)
findings.consequence: grain is NOT monotone in compression - content already below digital 55 gets CLEANER when compressed harder

findings.claim: THE WHITE-POINT KNEE IS AT 0.75, BRACKETED ON BOTH SIDES BY MEASUREMENTS THAT CLEAR THE BARS
findings.robustness: re-derived all 48 tonefine rows with alignment forced to (0.98,+72,-28): knee unchanged, every detail metric still tied between 0.75 and 0.64, all three grain metrics still clear
findings.independently_confirms: ADR-093 (ship a single white-point of ~0.75) from a different measurement sharing no data

findings.claim: (wp 0.75, gamma 1.0) Pareto-dominates every other cell tested
findings.consequence: once white-point is at 0.75, gamma above 1.0 is a pure cost on the neutral ramp: no measurable highlight recovery (0.40->0.82, bar 1.30), +12.6 highlight grain, -57 luminance
findings.scope: neutral ramp only - says nothing about colour

findings.claim: Gamma buys the same detail in a worse currency and does not finish the job
findings.confirms: ADR-090 (gamma preserves endpoints so the top still clips) - now with an error bar

findings.claim: Chroma-gamma and saturation are exact no-ops on a neutral ramp, over the FULL lever range
findings.method_warning: the null MUST be evaluated on the quantised output of a pre-fed generator. Applying the lever chain to the ALREADY-DITHERED target reports saturation 0.7 changing 41% of grid-band pixels by up to 68/255 - an artefact of the test
findings.consequence: this is what licenses A1's identical-render replicate groups, hence every error bar in the corpus

findings.claim: Work 16 (Flaming June) is a REAL anomaly - a registered prediction FAILED
findings.prediction: if the grain ridge explains it, work 16 must be dark with little above the ceiling; ADR-092 predicts the opposite (bright)

outcome.but: 3rd darkest of 12; the two DARKER works both picked 0.88

candidates_not_testable_here: work 16 is 2nd highest mean_chroma (86.5, median 41.5) and highest chroma_stddev (43.3) - may be CHROMA noise, invisible to a neutral ramp (B2 territory)
0.64-pickers average lum_stddev 45.8 vs 0.88-pickers 32.8 (n=7,8, no test performed)

findings.claim: Round 4 shifted toward LESS compression - an observation, NOT a re-decision of ADR-093
The DIGITAL palette transfer function - exact, needs no rig - is the object that answers both collapses
findings.consequence: black crush is not a cliff in the mean, it is a DILUTION of what the tone is made of. Exact mirror of ADR-091 at the other end: one ink below 71, one above 101

findings.claim: The MEASURED rig transfer is a genuine transfer function in level alone - but the rig cannot resolve tone below digital 40, where the render says there is tone
findings.unresolved: PANEL or CAMERA cannot be separated - no reflectance standard in frame, and ADR-090 already recorded the camera exaggerating collapse (input 112 vs 159)
findings.do_not_say: 'the panel crushes everything below digital 40' - the honest statement is that the RIG cannot resolve it

findings.claim: An S-curve CAN do what no power function can - and the arithmetic needs no rig
findings.structural: a power function fixes both endpoints (0->0, 255->255) so it always trades one collapse for the other; a scale moves the top and drags the bottom down in proportion; only a two-free-endpoint map can place both ends inside the usable window [~40,163]
costs: the shadow lift deposits content at digital 60-90, and the measured grain ridge peaks at 55 - NightWatch predicted grain 27.5 -> 34.1

a black point lifted to digital 80 means the image contains NO BLACK at all; the black ink is the one place this panel is unambiguously good. That is a judge question (ADR-084), not a measurement question
on Olympia the S-curve is a Pareto improvement (0% black, 0% clip, grain 20.2 < 22.9) because its mass is already above the ridge
findings.untestable_here: no corpus condition has a non-power shape, and the readout built for worming (anisotropy) was ruled unusable by A1

findings.claim: linepairs: Floyd-Steinberg loses NOTHING; the entire measured roll-off is the rig
findings.overturns: the expected DIAGONAL penalty from FS direction bias does not exist - digitally the diagonal is the BEST preserved orientation (1.000 at every period vs 0.80-0.99 vertical)
findings.no_lever_finding: one row per setting and `retained` normalises against a 48px reference the levers themselves move

findings.consequence: the ~41% modulation deficit is panel+camera+registration; 'the resampler ate it before the dither saw it' is ruled out
findings.not_a_finding: the ~13-unit scale-4 deficit has no replicate and therefore no bar

findings.claim: surround: no surround term above the noise, but the target cannot prove it
findings.design_flaw: target_surround assigns its 25 surrounds in INDEX ORDER, so surround value is perfectly confounded with grid position - the black and near-black surrounds are cells 0 and 1, the top-left corner, exactly where registration fails
findings.fix: shuffle the surround assignment across the grid and take three replicates - three refreshes

unresolved: PANEL vs CAMERA at the shadow end - no reflectance standard in frame
the +26/255 grid-row term - row and level are perfectly confounded within a condition
work 16 - a registered prediction failed; likely chroma, which B1 does not own
edges - the asymmetry question, in either direction
linepairs - any lever effect (moving normaliser, n=1 per setting)
surround - value vs position (design confound, no replicate)
worming under an S-curve - anisotropy is unusable
grain_peak and ramp_span are not recoverable from this corpus at all

recommendations.what: white-point 0.75, gamma 1.0 on the neutral-tone evidence; it Pareto-dominates every alternative tested and independently confirms ADR-093
a shadow target mirroring tonefine to input 0-100; a reflectance standard in frame to divide out the camera toe; at least one non-power curve condition; a gamma axis that includes values below 1.0

what: re-place readout_edges' strips on the same-polarity transition (defect #10)
shuffle target_surround's surround assignment across the grid
sample the calibration strip on corrected-before-align (A1's defect #8) - still the highest-value one-line fix
